title: Does Cursor Remember Your Project?
script: I gave Cursor four project rules, then opened a fresh agent. Use this package manager. Reuse this button. Keep dark mode. Run the UI test. The new task never repeated those instructions. I asked for a settings page. I inspected the commands, imports, theme behavior, and test run. Reading the rules is not the same as following them. It followed [RULES_FOLLOWED] of four rules. [MISSED_RULE_OR_CLEAN_RUN]. [RULES_VS_MEMORY_CONCLUSION]. Would you put your project conventions here?
timingStatus: Aligned to actual Voicebox recording with local recognized word timestamps. Minor unrecognized tokens interpolate between recognized neighbors.
concept: Test package manager, existing button, dark-mode and UI-test recall.
whyNow: AI coding and automation promises are judged by a reproducible useful task.
viewerGoal: Understand what the system actually completed and where supervision matters.
hooks: I gave Cursor four project rules, then opened a fresh agent.
The new agent gets four rules. Does it follow them?
Persistent instructions are not magic memory. Let us check.
strongestHook: I gave Cursor four project rules, then opened a fresh agent.
directorBrief: Direct this as an observable challenge: Test package manager, existing button, dark-mode and UI-test recall. The viewer must see the starting problem, the exact constraint, one revealing action and the independently checked output. Let the real failure or correction create the turn. Save every first attempt. Completion claims alone never establish a result.
effort: 15–60 minutes core build/test; allow additional audit/edit time.
protocol: Use supported Cursor project rules explicitly, not an unverified memory feature. Put four scoped conventions in the real project rules: use the existing package manager, import the existing Button, preserve dark mode, run the named UI test. Capture rule file and scope. Start a fresh agent and ask only for a settings page with one save action. Inspect package commands, imports, theme behavior and actual test execution. Compare rule application to observed work; do not infer learning from persistent instructions.
evidenceRequirements: Confirm feature access; audit all four rules in a fresh task.
